why: W24 (APP_PLAN §6 row W24; readiness gap G10). The capability entity is declared as 'the bridge between the syllabus and the exam' and carries four fields: id, level, name, grammar_keys. There is no can-do statement, no field that reaches the exam, and no kind that can express vocabulary, so build_capabilities.py maps 266 of 322 lessons and corpus/capabilities/exemptions.json carries the other 56 (42 of them as pending-capability-design, 34 of those N3). This table proposes the kinds, the mapping rules, the can-do text and the exam link. PROPOSAL ONLY: no repo code, contract or lesson was edited.
definition: capabilities[] is the full replacement registry (125 rows = the 74 that ship today, unchanged in id/level/grammar_keys, plus 51 new ones). `kind` is the new enum. `can_do` is Layer C, authored from the lessons' objectives quoted verbatim in `can_do_derived_from`, and every row is ai_generated + needs_review. `exam_link` is derived from the bank items' own provenance (rule R-EXAMLINK); an empty array means the corpus genuinely assesses that capability nowhere. `lesson_map` is the full 322-lesson map; `lesson_map_first_time` are the 56 lessons that map to a capability for the first time. Apply order: land the schema, run the builder with the new rules, empty exemptions.json, then re-run validate_capabilities + validate_graph_edges.
generated: 2026-09-10, by the W24 derivation over a scratch copy of db/corpus.sqlite + the committed export at HEAD (2626d20c).

kinds.grammar: A group of grammar points the learner can deploy. Curated groups plus a topic-bucket fallback; the 72 capabilities that ship today, unchanged.
kinds.script: A writing system the learner can read: kana, kanji, and the romaji support that pre-N5 leans on before kana is fluent.
kinds.vocabulary: A lexical field the learner can name. NEW in W24: it is what the 42 vocabulary-only lessons unlock, and what corpus/capabilities/exemptions.json carried 42 pending-capability-design entries for.
kinds.phonology: A property of the sound system the learner can produce or hear. NEW in W24: the pre-N5 sound and pronunciation lessons unlock no corpus item, so no unlock-derived rule could ever reach them.
kinds.exam-readiness: The consolidated claim a review topic makes: the learner can sit the level's paper. NEW in W24; it is the only capability kind whose exam_link is the whole paper rather than the items its own material produced.
kinds.study-method: How to use the course and its review engine. NEW in W24, and the only kind that is not a language capability: it exists so that les:pre-n5-orientacao-01 maps to what it actually teaches instead of to nothing.

rules.rule: Every `vocab` unlock maps to cap:vocab:<topic-slug>, where the topic is the topic of the LESSON that unlocks the word. A lesson receives one vocabulary capability per distinct topic among its vocab unlocks (in practice always its own).
rules.why: It mirrors the rule already used for grammar (introducing-topic bucket) and for kanji (every lesson with a kanji unlock gets cap:kanji-recognition), so vocabulary stops being the one unlock type that maps to nothing. The unlocking lesson is the only usable source: vocab.introducing_topic_id is NULL for 2,912 of the 2,945 unlocked words and agrees with the lesson's topic on all 33 where it is set (0 disagreements).

rules.rule: Curated: the lessons of top:pre-n5-sons and top:pre-n5-pronuncia, plus les:pre-n5-orientacao-02, split into cap:phonology-segments (vowels, consonants, devoicing) and cap:phonology-mora (mora count, long vowels, っ, ん, pitch).
rules.why: These lessons unlock no corpus item by design, so no derivation from unlocks can reach them. The split follows what the lessons actually teach, and it is curated the same way the 44 grammar groups in build_capabilities.CAPS already are.

rules.rule: cap:romaji-reading is added and mapped to les:pre-n5-orientacao-02, alongside the existing cap:kana-reading and cap:kanji-recognition.
rules.why: Romaji is a script the course explicitly teaches to read and then withdraws; two of that lesson's three objectives are about reading it correctly.

The lesson teaches the course structure and spaced repetition. Its objectives are can-do shaped and testable, but nothing linguistic is unlocked, so no other kind fits. Naming the kind honestly is better than carrying the lesson as an exemption forever.

rules.rule: Every lesson whose topic slug matches top:<level>-revisao maps to cap:exam-readiness-<level>.
rules.why: Derived from the topic slug, so it is mechanical and it extends to N3 the moment W22 grows top:n3-revisao from one lesson to three. It is also the capability the exam simulator's own feature unlock (feat:jlpt-sim-n5 / -n4) belongs to.

rules.rule: exam_link[] is derived per item: item.grammar -> the capability owning that grammar key; item.vocab -> cap:vocab:<topic of the unlocking lesson>, plus cap:kanji-recognition when the section is kanji_reading or orthography; item.reading -> reading.gated_to_lesson -> every capability of that lesson; otherwise item.sentence -> sentence_grammar keys -> their capabilities. Rows are aggregated to (level, section) with an item count. An exam-readiness capability instead links to every section its level's paper spec draws from.
rules.why: It is the only link the data can justify: it reads the provenance the bank builder already wrote, so nothing is asserted that an item does not itself carry.

schema_fragment.target: contracts/capability.schema.json (regenerated by scripts/contracts/build_schemas.py from contracts/_shapes.json) + design/courseware_architecture.md
schema_fragment.note: Additive. `id`, `level`, `name` and `grammar_keys` keep their current shape and stay required; `grammar_keys` becomes an empty array on every non-grammar kind, which it already is on cap:kana-reading and cap:kanji-recognition today.

kind.description: What sort of thing the learner can do. Neutral English, not localized. Vocabulary owner: design: design/courseware_architecture.md. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

can_do.description: One first-person sentence naming an observable act the learner can perform once this capability's lessons are done. Layer C, authored from the lessons' own objectives, needs_review. This is the field design/learning_science.md R66 requires before R65 can ship: the capability's `name` is a syllabus label, not a can-do.

can_do_evidence.description: The weakest evidence that licenses asserting this can_do to a learner. R67: a recognition-only FSRS state may not produce 'você já consegue', so a capability whose exercises are recognition-only declares `recognition` and the app must phrase it as 'você já reconhece'.

can_do_derived_from.description: The lesson objectives the can_do was authored from, quoted verbatim. Makes the Layer-C claim auditable without re-reading the lessons.

lessons.description: The lessons that introduce this capability. The inverse of corpus/capabilities/lesson_map.json, stored so a consumer can walk capability -> lesson without loading the map.

exam_link.description: Where this capability is assessed. One row per (level, section) of the exam banks, with the number of bank items whose own provenance reaches this capability. This is the field contracts/manifest.json already promises when it calls a capability 'the bridge between the syllabus and the exam'.

section.description: The bank type, exactly as design/exam_simulator.md names it: kanji_reading, orthography, context_fill, grammar_form, sentence_order, paraphrase, usage, text_grammar, reading_comp, listening_task, listening_point, listening_gist, listening_say, listening_reply.

bank.description: Path of the bank file the section reads.

via.description: item-provenance = derived from the items' own vocab/grammar/reading/sentence refs. paper = the whole-paper link an exam-readiness capability carries.

validator_changes: validate_capabilities.py: add (a) `kind` present and in the enum; (b) `can_do['pt-BR']` non-empty on every capability; (c) every can_do_derived_from.lesson resolves AND is in that capability's lesson list; (d) EVERY lesson in `lesson` is a key of lesson_map.json, so the exemptions file is no longer needed to keep the gate green; (e) exam_link rows name a bank file that exists and a (level, section) the paper spec knows.
validate_graph_edges.py capability_coverage: keep the unmapped-lesson check, but read it against 0 exemptions rather than 56.

corpus/capabilities/exemptions.json: drops from 56 entries to 0. Its `why` text says an entry that no longer matches anything is itself a hard failure, so the file must be emptied in the same commit that lands the kinds.
